summary: Kuno Meyer (1858–1919) was a linguist who studied under Ernst Windisch at the University of Leipzig (~1879–1883). He held posts at the University of Liverpool (~1884–1911) and the University of Berlin (~1911–1919), where he succeeded Heinrich Zimmer in 1911.

Working in philosophy and Buddhist studies, Kuntala Bhattacharya earned an MA under Prabal Kumar Sen and a PhD at Jadavpur University under Amita Chatterjee and Shyamapada Misra (attested 2009). She held a post at Rabindra Bharati University (attested 2009).
Kunzang Namgyal studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

Kunzang Pelden studied under Patrul Rinpoche, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and Khenpo Shenga. His students included Shechen Gyaltsab, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Dodrupchen Rinpoche, and Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen.

Kurt A. Behrendt (born 1964) specializes in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. After completing his PhD at UCLA (~1991–1997), he served at the Metropolitan Museum of Art as Assistant Curator (~2002–2012) and Associate Curator of South Asian Art (~2012).
Kurt Andrew Johnson is a scholar in Indology who completed his PhD at the University of York in 2010 under the supervision of Jane Moody.

Kurt Huber (1893–1943) was a philosopher educated at Eberhard-Ludwigs-Gymnasium and the University of Munich, where he completed his PhD (~1913–1917) and Habilitation (~1917–1920). He held an extraordinary professorship (1926) and a professorship (1938) at the University of Munich.

Kurt Tropper works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his doctorate at the University of Vienna in 2001 under Ernst Steinkellner, having also studied under Michael Torsten Much and Tashi Geisler, and held posts at Vienna and the Austrian Academy of Sciences.

Kurtis R. Schaeffer works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. After studying at Lewis & Clark, Evergreen State, the University of Washington (MA ~1992–1995), and Harvard (PhD ~1995–2000), he held posts at the University of Alabama (2000, 2004) and the University of Virginia (2005).
Kurunegoda Piyatissa (1929–2012) was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as the head of the New York Buddhist Vihara (attested 1998 and 2009).

Kwangsoo Park specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed an MA at the University of Iowa, a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, and served as a professor at Wonkwang University (attested 2020).

Kyo Kano works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Keio University, Kyoto University, and the University of Vienna, and held posts as an assistant at Kyoto University (attested 1989) and associate professor at Kobe Women's University (attested 2000).

Kyojun Shimizutani (1891–1979) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Keijun Shimizutani, at Tendai Sect University, and Taisho University. He held professorships at Tendai Sect University (1919) and Taisho University (1926–1945), and was abbot of Senso-ji (~1953–1979).

Kyoko Fujii (born 1948) studied at the University of Tokyo (~1968–1977). A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, she held professorships at Yokohama City, Hamamatsu, Hokkaido, and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, later directing the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.
Kyoko Tokuno is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She held a post at the University of Oregon and served as a professor at the University of Washington (attested 2017).
Kyokuga Saeki (1828–1891) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under numerous traditional teachers, including Gen'yu, Reiga, and Ryoki Noyama. He served as the 143rd elder of Sennyu-ji.

Kyosho Hayashima (1914–1999) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He held teaching posts at Yokohama City University (attested 1962), Toyo University (attested 1962), and the University of Tokyo (attested 1980).
Kyosho Tanaka (born 1947) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1970–1976). He served as an associate professor at Musashino University (~1976–2012).
Kyoshun Todo (1916–2002) was a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at Bukkyo University as an associate professor (attested 1962) and as a professor (attested 1988–1992).

Kyozan Joshu Sasaki (1907–2014) was a Buddhist master who studied at Zuiryo-ji and Myoshin-ji, training under Joten Soko Miura (~1928–1953). He served as abbot of Yotoku-in, Shojuan, and the Mount Baldy Zen Center, which he founded.
